newsitem.title: USA: Information tech mergers top $164 bln in 96 - study.
newsitem.headline: Information tech mergers top $164 bln in 96 - study.

text.p: The total value of mergers and acquisitions within the North American information technology industry grew to $164.6 billion in 1996, up from $82.8 billion in 1995, according to a study released Tuesday by consulting firm Broadview Associates.
The firm forecast that 72 percent of North American information technology companies are likely to pursue mergers or acquisitions over the next 12 months, up from 64 percent last year.
Broadview, in its 1996 Year-End Merger and Acquisition Report, said there were a record 1,962 mergers in 1996, up from 1,563 transactions in 1995.

"The growth in M&A transaction value in 1996 was largely the result of some major deals by big players that pumped up valuations in many sectors," Charlie Federman, chairman of Broadview Associates, said in a statement.
For example, he said, in the telecommunications sector, four transactions accounted for $70.7 billion in value.
Globally, IT merger transactions totaled 3,342 in 1996, up 15 percent from 2,913 in 1995, while transaction value increased to $234.2 billion, versus $134.0 billion in 1995.

Rapid changes in technology fueled the North American merger and acqusition surge in 1996, with IT companies reacting to heightened market expectations and competitive pressure to accelerate product innovation and delivery.

"This creates opportunities for both large companies as well (as) the niche players," Federman said. "Small companies need access to distribution channels controlled by large companies, and large companies need access to technology developed by nimble small companies."

M&A activity in 1996 reflects IT companies' shift away from diversification in favor of building on core capabilities, Broadview said. Further, many moves were driven by concentration, with a predominance of transactions involving competitors or directly complementary products.
Active sectors in 1996 included telecommunications, supporting products and services, hardware and software products and media and content services.
